p.seg: De armonica consideratione Boetius ita disseruit:
Quia neque solum in terminis speculationem proporcionis habet, neque solum in differentiis, sed in utrisque communiter,
querit enim ut quemadmodum sunt ad se extremi termini, sic maioris ad medium differentia contra differentiam medietatis ad ultimum.
Concerning the harmonic relationship, Boethius stated thus:
Because it exhibits a proportional relationship not only between the terms, nor only between their differences, but between both jointly,
it requires that just as the extreme terms are to each other, so too is the difference between the greater term and the mean as compared with the difference between the mean and the lesser term.
Ipsarum quoque musicarum consonantiarum, quas symphonias nominant, proporciones in hac poene sola medietate frequenter inuenies.
Namque symphonia diatesseron que princeps est et quodammodo uim obtinet elementi, in eiusmodi armonicis medietatibus inuenitur, ut sunt VI ad VIII
You will also frequently find the proportions of the musical consonances themselves, which they call symphonies, almost solely in this mean.
For the diatessaron consonance, which is the principal [consonance], and holds the force of an element in a certain way, is found in harmonic means of this type, as 6 is to 8.
Sunt ergo huiusmodi medietatis termini, quorum extremi sint dupli, et alii quorum extremi sint tripli, ita:
Duodenarius igitur ad senarium duplus est;
et in alia dispositione XII ad IIII triplus est.
Horum diferentias colligamus et ad se inuicem comparemus, epytrita proportio, id est diatesseron symphonia colligitur.
Inter VI enim et XII senarius est, et inter IIII et XII octonarius;
qui scilicet octonarius ad senarium sesquiterciam efficit proportionem.
There are terms of a harmonic mean of this type, whose extremes are duple, and others whose extremes are triple, thus:
Therefore, 12 to 6 is a duple,
and in the other disposition 12 to 4 is triple;
if we take the differences of these and compare them with each other, an epitrita proportion, that is a diatessaron consonance, is formed.
For between 6 and 12 is a 6, and between 4 and twelve
an 8, which 8 of course makes a sesquitertian proportion to the six.
In eadem quoque medietate et diapente symphonia componitur.
In duplici, uidelicet XII ad VIII et in triplici VI ad IIII sesqualtera est.
In the same mean, moreover, a diapente consonance is composed.
In the duple, 12 to 8, and in the triple, 6 to 4, there is clearly a sesquialtera.
Post hunc autem diapason consonantia est, ut VI ad XII.
In triplici quoque dispositione simul diapente et diapason symphonia componitur, ut sunt
After this, however, there is a diapason consonance, as [for example] 6 to 12.
In the triple disposition, moreover, the consonance of both a diapente and diapason is composed at the same time, as are
Et quoniam triplus duas continet consonantias, diapente scilicet ac diapason, in differentiis eiusdem triplicis eundem triplum reperiemus.
Nam inter VI et VIIII ternarius differentia est, et inter VIII. et XVIII nouenarius, qui ad ternarium triplus est.
And since the triple [disposition] contains two consonances, namely the diapente and the diapason, we shall discover the same triple relationship in the differences of this same triple [disposition].
For between 6 and 9 the difference is three. And between 9 and 18 nine, which is a triple in relation to three.
In dupla vero proportione, major terminus differentiam sui et medii termini triplus est,
et rursus minor terminus ad differentiam sui et medii termini triplus est.
Nam inter VIII. et XII. quaternarius est, qui ad eundem duodenarium triplus est, et inter VI. et VIII. binarius, qui rursus ad eundem senarium triplus est.
In the duple disposition, however, the greater term is three times the difference of the mean term as compared with itself,
and likewise the lesser term is three times its difference from the mean term.
